issue.title: `gh issue close` can also close and comment pull requests
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`gh version 2.20.2 (2022-11-15)`

As a part of cleanup before closing an old, unmaintained repository I decided to close the old, but still opened issues.   
I was very confused when it appeared that command:   
`gh issue close https://github.com/project/repo/issues/NUMBER -c "example message" -r "not planned"`   
can also close unclosed pull request and comment closed ones.

It happens only with links, which are redirected to pull requests (I don't know why).  
For example `https://github.com/AntiMicro/antimicro/issues/273` is redirected to `https://github.com/AntiMicro/antimicro/pull/273`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use command `gh issue close https://github.com/AntiMicro/antimicro/issues/273 -c "Closing" -r "not planned"`

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected:  
I should get either an error or message informing that this is PR, not an issue, or at least info, that this PR is already closed.   

Actual:   
If PR is closed, then only comment is published, if PR is open commend is published and it is closed.

### Logs

comments.body:
I agree that this inconsistency is confusing, but it has less to do with `gh` and more to do with the surprising fact that PRs and Issues share an ID space. There is one "thing" with number 273 and, because of architectural decisions made long ago, `issues/273` can be treated the same way as `pull/273`. Indeed, if I try and follow https://github.com/AntiMicro/antimicro/issues/273 in the browser github.com happily redirects to the pull request page instead. To this end, `gh issue close` and `gh pr close` actually share most of the same codepath.

We _could_ patch this to do an extra check in `issue close` to ensure strictness but I'm not sure it's worth the extra request and lean towards leaving things the way they are (especially because other users have specifically requested to _always_ treat issues and prs as the same thing)
comments.author: vilmibm

comments.body:
Also note that `gh issue close <issue>` used to only work on Issues, but we expanded it to also work for Pull Requests since, as Nate explains, Issues and PRs are for most part interchangeable. This was done because sometimes users just want to use gh to close `#123` or to comment on `#123` without knowing if `#123` is an Issue or Pull Request. https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/4794

If you need to absolutely ensure that you only close issue `#273` but never a PR `#273`, you need to first perform diligence to check the type of the resource you are referencing. To check if something is a PR, you can use `gh pr view <number> --json url`, which will error out for non-PR arguments.
comments.author: mislav

comments.body:
But in the case when I directly state, that it should be marked as `not planned` we can assume, that I am thinking about closing an Issue, not PR.    
Such a generalization can be useful. I think it could be linked with another flag like `--only-issues`, which would prevent interacting with no-issues.
comments.author: pktiuk

comments.body:
After some more deliberation, I don't think it's likely that we will either change this behavior or add a new flag such as `--only-issues`. I do not see the utility in that for most users.

If you need to comment or close `#NUMBER` while ensuring that NUMBER only refers to issues and not pull requests, you can use the workaround I suggested in my previous comment.
